title: SharePoint and OneDrive: updated search experience with Copilot Search
summary: Hold: the licensing field applies an included entitlement to the SharePoint and OneDrive experience using documentation explicitly limited to the Copilot app. The rollout dates, required action, default arrival and listed control paths are supported. Two existing-control descriptions also need qualifications from their current documentation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: The control is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.where: controls[1].api
claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Open PowerShell as an administrator and run the following command:
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Learn documents neither an admin UI path nor an automation command for deferring this updated search experience.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint OneDrive Copilot Search defer tenant site opt out Set-SPOTenant Set-SPOSite search experience'; opened Search manage, admin experience, FAQ and both cmdlet references; searched their text for search, Copilot and defer. No deferral operation found.

claims.where: controls[1].scope and note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing site-level discovery control, not the announced search-interface deferral switch.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting. When you turn on the setting, Microsoft 365 search systems propagate it so that content from the site doesn't appear in organization-wide discovery experiences.

claims.where: Governance controls: Restricted Content Discovery explanation
claims.claim: Learn says restricted sites do not appear in organisation-wide search and Copilot answers unless the user owns or recently interacted with content.
claims.quote: This setting prevents these sites from appearing in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot answers unless a user owns or has recently interacted with content on those sites.
claims.fix: Add: 'The Restricted Content Discovery page describes limiting discovery including recently interacted files, whereas the Copilot Search management page states an ownership or recent-interaction exception; these descriptions differ.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery alongside the existing management source.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery affects organisation-wide search experiences such as SharePoint home and Microsoft Copilot discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect searches originating from site context.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect searches that originate from site context or other intelligent experiences such as Microsoft 365 Feed and Recommendations.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn describes Restricted Content Discovery as a temporary governance control while permissions are reviewed.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is designed as a temporary governance control that gives organizations time to review and right-size access while continuing their Copilot deployment.
